hook.en: A start-up with a clever idea but no profits cannot easily issue debentures or get a bank loan. Yet many such start-ups raise crores. Who gives them money, and on what terms?

objectives.en: Distinguish angel investors and venture capitalists

narration.en: A start-up with a clever idea but no profits cannot easily issue debentures or get a bank loan. Yet many such start-ups raise crores. Who gives them money, and on what terms?

body.en: A global depository receipt (GDR) is a negotiable instrument issued abroad by a depository bank and backed by shares of an Indian company held in custody in India; it lets the company raise foreign currency from investors in other countries, and the GDR is traded on a foreign stock exchange. Angel investors are wealthy individuals who invest their own money in very early-stage start-ups, usually in exchange for equity, and often also give advice and contacts. Venture capitalists are professional funds that invest pooled money in young, high-risk, high-growth companies, take an equity stake and a role on the board, and exit after some years, often through a public issue or a sale.

points.en: GDR: foreign funds through receipts backed by shares
Angel investors: individuals, early stage, small amounts
Venture capital: professional funds, larger amounts, active role, planned exit

title.en: On the board: Modern sources at a glance

say.en: Five modern sources, who provides the money and what they get.

body.en: Crowdfunding raises small amounts from a large number of people through an online platform. It may be donation-based, reward-based (backers get the product or a gift) or equity-based where the law allows. It also tests whether people want the product. Peer-to-peer (P2P) lending uses an online platform to match borrowers directly with individual lenders, without a bank in between; in India P2P platforms are registered as NBFCs and regulated by the RBI. These sources are flexible and fast, but they carry high risk for investors and may be costly for borrowers.

points.en: P2P lending: individuals lend to borrowers via a platform
P2P platforms in India: NBFC-P2P regulated by the RBI

problem.en: A start-up runs a 30-day reward-based campaign for ₹20 lakh. The average pledge is ₹800. It gets 120 backers a day in week 1, 40 a day for the next 14 days and 90 a day in the last 9 days. Is the goal reached? If not, how many more backers are needed?

answer.en: Not reached: about 290 more backers (₹2.32 lakh) are needed, so the start-up must promote harder near the deadline.

body.en: Angels invest their own money at the idea stage; venture capitalists invest pooled funds once the business shows it can grow.

narration.en: Angel early, VC later. Angels invest their own money at the idea stage; venture capitalists invest pooled funds once the business shows it can grow.
